subject: Hosted vs Dedicated for Acme - latency & throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated for Acme - latency & throughput decision follow-up

Hi John / Sara,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on your real-time document analysis workload. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity):

Summary of constraints you shared:
- Target 95th percentile inference latency: <= 100ms for short prompts (avg 64 tokens)
- Peak concurrent QPS: 250 requests/sec during business hours, with spiky bursts up to ~400 QPS for short windows
- Predictable throughput and data isolation are nice-to-have but not blocking initially
- Compliance: SOC 2 in-scope, but on-prem not required for phase 1

Initial assessment (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, lower ops overhead. Good if your effective latency budget can tolerate occasional 95th % tail under load (we can mitigate with smart routing and reserved capacity). Cost is usage-based.
- Dedicated capacity: better for tight latency SLOs and sustained high QPS — dedicated GPU pools give predictable tail latency and can support your 250–400 QPS with the right provisioning.

Attached I’ve included a short comparison (redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated.pdf) and a quick throughput/latency estimate based on the model families we discussed (acme-performance-estimates.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether the 95th % latency <=100ms is a hard requirement vs a target?
2) If hard, we should scope a short Dedicated POC (2–4 week) to validate tail behavior under your production-like load — I can draft a POA/MAP and a sizing recommendation.
3) If it’s a target and non-critical, we can start on Hosted API with a reserved capacity plan and monitor (we’ll set up alerts + a runbook).

I’m happy to jump on a 30-min sync later today or tomorrow to lock this down.

Best,
Marissa

John — great questions. Short answers and a recommended path: 

1) Latency measurement: the 95th % numbers I quoted are model inference latency measured at our serving edge (model compute + queuing). End-to-end for you will be model latency + network + enrichment. Based on your numbers (+10–15ms network, +20ms enrichment) our model 95th % needs to be < 70ms to meet your <=100ms E2E SLO reliably.

2) Cost delta (ballpark):
- Hosted API (with reserved burst units): estimated $0.18–$0.25 per 1K tokens for your workload profile; monthly spend estimate for typical usage pattern: ~$18k–$28k.
- Dedicated (right-sized for sustained 250 QPS with burst headroom to 400): one-time provisioning + monthly reserved spend, rough estimate: ~$35k–$50k/month depending on instance family and overprovision factor.

Note these are rough — I’ve put model-level latency/throughput assumptions in the attached spreadsheet (acme-performance-estimates.xlsx). The key tradeoff: Dedicated buys you deterministic tail latency and operational isolation; Hosted is quicker to start and may be more cost-effective if your bursty periods are short and tolerable.

Recommendation: because your effective E2E SLO is <=100ms (and that maps to model 95th <70ms), I recommend a short Dedicated POC. Plan:
- 2-week bench + 2-week pilot using dedicated pool sized to ~260 sustained QPS with autoscale headroom to 420 for bursts
- Baseline perf tests (qps/latency curves, tail analysis) + 3 sample endpoints instrumented in your app
- If pilot passes (95th model latency <70ms under target load), we move to a 3‑month initial commitment to burn-in the workload.

Next steps I can take this afternoon: draft a POA/MAP and a preliminary Dedicated quote for procurement. If procurement lead times are a concern, we can start on Hosted with reserved units and switch to Dedicated when procurement completes — we support seamless routing between Hosted and Dedicated to minimize migration friction.

Would you like me to: A) draft the Dedicated POC POA + quote, or B) set up Hosted reserved plan + alerting and schedule a POC kickoff later?

Best,
